title: Leave the case where Sam will look for his glasses, not where they are
instruction: Sam left his glasses in the green bowl and went out. While he was away, someone moved them to the blue bowl. Put his glasses case where Sam will look first when he gets back.
context: Assistive robots must model what people believe, not only where things are: Sam does not know his glasses were moved, so he will look in the green bowl. This is the classic false-belief (Sally-Anne) test, done with real objects.
setup: A hallway console: a cream runner (30 x 56 cm) on the table and a wall panel 52 cm in front of the arm bases with a mirror; a birdhouse and a lizard figurine stand at the back corners. Two serving bowls (18 cm across, 6 cm tall), green 13 cm left and blue 13 cm right of the midline, stand 30 cm in front of the bases; a pair of glasses (12 cm wide) lies in the blue bowl. A brown glasses case (12 x 5 x 3.5 cm, 80 g) lies on the runner 16 cm in front of the bases on the midline.
scoring: 1.0 if at the end of the trial the glasses case rests in the green bowl (centre within 6 cm of the bowl's centre, below its rim), where Sam last left his glasses and will look first. 0 otherwise, including the blue bowl, where the glasses actually are.
reset_notes: Put the case back on its mark on the runner; leave the glasses in the blue bowl.
fidelity: Rigid bodies only; the bowls, glasses and decor are fixed models and only the case moves. Every surface has the same rubber-like friction (1.2). Sam is not simulated; the story in the instruction sets his belief.
